proof_scope: An exact zero bulk moment up to O(q^(-1/2)) for the quadratic Jacobi column T2 minus its signed transform constrains the actual stationary solution. At t=1 the resulting reciprocal Cauchy-Schwarz bound gives limsup |m| <= log(22731/20000) < .128 on all eligible primes and squares. Its constant has a rational polynomial certificate.

A reciprocal compact model at m=log(57/50) meets all affine moment constraints from round 41. The entire positive quadratic test family still permits compact subintervals of the elementary cold mark range at small t. The model does not satisfy the full Fourier constraints.

For any sequence of square floors t_q down to zero, the loss log(theta_-/P_{-,0}(t_q)) divided by t_q has limsup strictly below .105. The prime analogue on either side requires log(theta_sigma/L_sigma)=o(t_q). Neither estimate controls a common complex domain.

For every actual feasible witness a finite kinetic-plus-reciprocal action inequality improves the critical surplus coefficient by 3 pi^(2/3). It remains valid at shrinking positive floor and asymptotically gives this coefficient when gamma_+ = o((tau/T)^(1/3)). The on-root square subfield case at tau=1 gives the actual lower coefficient 3 pi^(2/3) 2^(-1/6) inside the short mark window.

The actual translated signed endpoint score has negative part O(sqrt(t)) pointwise and an exceptional fraction bound simultaneous over all t>=L. An adaptive grid and dyadic L2 argument sharpen the latter to O(W(1+log(2/eta))^2/(eta^2 L)). This allows the distinguished root to remain exceptional and neither gives a prime rooted upper estimate nor treats the critical T^(1/3) scale.
